sections.title: How My Jeevan Anand Calculator Works (The Math Behind the Magic)

content.text: I built this calculator to pull back the curtain on how LIC's returns are actually calculated. It's not a black box. It combines the guaranteed parts with the variable bonuses to give you a projection you can actually understand.

The Maturity Formula: SA + Vested Bonus + FAB

At its heart, the calculation for your final payout is this simple formula:

Maturity Value = Sum Assured + Vested Bonuses + Final Additional Bonus (FAB)

Let me show you with a real example. For a ₹10 Lakh policy over 25 years (with an illustrative bonus rate of ₹45 and FAB of ₹100 per ₹1000 SA):

  • Sum Assured: This is the guaranteed part, your base: ₹10,00,000
  • Vested Bonus: This is the big variable. My math: (10,00,000 / 1000) * 45 * 25 = ₹11,25,000
  • FAB (Loyalty Bonus): Your reward for staying long-term: (10,00,000 / 1000) * 100 = ₹1,00,000
  • Your Total Estimated Payout: ₹10,00,000 + ₹11,25,000 + ₹1,00,000 = ₹22,25,000

Where do the bonus & FAB numbers come from?

Here's the honest truth: bonuses aren't guaranteed. Anyone who tells you otherwise is selling something. My calculator uses illustrative rates taken directly from analyzing LIC's past bonus declarations. For the official-but-less-clear version, you can always see the LIC New Jeevan Anand brochure.

sections.title: Inputs explained: DOB, Sum Assured, Term, Premium, Bonus per ₹1,000, FAB

items: Age & Term: These are the two biggest factors that decide your premium. The younger you start, the cheaper it is. Simple.
Sum Assured: This is the guaranteed death benefit and the base for your maturity calculation. It's the 'promise' of the policy.
Bonus per ₹1,000: This is where the real growth happens. It's the Simple Reversionary Bonus rate. A historical average of ₹40-₹49 is a realistic starting point for your estimates.

Final Additional Bonus (FAB): Think of this as a loyalty bonus for not giving up on your policy. It's paid at the end for long-term policies. You can leave this at 0 if you're unsure, but I've pre-filled a typical rate.

sections.title: Surrender & Paid-up values (formulas, GSV vs SSV, sample calc)

content.text: Thinking of stopping your premiums? This is a critical decision. You have two main options, and choosing the wrong one can cost you dearly. Let's break it down so you can make the right call.

items: Paid-Up Value: If you've paid for at least 2 years, you can just stop. The policy doesn't die. It becomes 'Paid-Up' with a lower Sum Assured. You'll still get a payout at the end. My calculator estimates this for you.

Surrender Value: This is where you terminate the policy completely and take a one-time cash payment. You lose the life cover. The value is split into Guaranteed (GSV) and Special (SSV). You always get the higher of the two, which is almost always the SSV. My calculator gives you a realistic estimate for this.

content.title: My Honest Advice: Surrender vs. Paid-up
content.text: If you don't need the cash urgently, making the policy 'Paid-Up' is almost always the smarter financial move. You keep some life cover and your money continues to grow. Only surrender if you have a dire, immediate cash need that you can't solve any other way.

sections.title: Jeevan Anand vs Popular Alternatives (Jeevan Labh, New Endowment)

rows: Goal-based savings with shorter pay commitment

content.text: My take: Jeevan Anand is unique because the life cover continues even after you get your maturity money. It's a 'two-in-one' for savings and leaving a legacy. Jeevan Labh is for people who want to finish paying premiums early. The New Endowment is the most basic, no-frills savings plan.

sections.title: Who should use this calculator & common use-cases (NRI, retiree, parent planning)

items: Parents Planning for the Future: I see many parents use this to plan for a child's education or marriage fund. It's a classic, safe choice.
Young Professionals: If you're looking for a disciplined long-term savings plan that also gives you life cover, this is a solid starting point.
NRIs Looking for Secure Indian Investments: Yes, NRIs can absolutely use this calculator. If you're looking for a safe, INR-denominated investment back home, this is one of the most popular options.

items.q: What is the LIC Jeevan Anand maturity formula?
items.a: The simple formula is: Maturity = Sum Assured + (Vested Bonus × Policy Term) + Final Additional Bonus (FAB). My calculator uses this exact logic to give you a clear estimate.

items.q: How to use the LIC Jeevan Anand calculator (Plan 715)?
items.a: It's easy. Just enter your age, the Sum Assured you want, and the policy term. I've pre-filled typical bonus rates to make it simpler. Click 'Calculate' to see your estimated premium, maturity, and surrender values instantly.

items.q: How accurate is an online Jeevan Anand calculator?
items.a: It is an estimate that depends on the bonus and FAB rates you input. Final maturity is determined by LIC and depends on declared bonuses and underwriting.

items.q: When does Jeevan Anand get surrender value?
items.a: Usually after 2 full years of premium payment; the Guaranteed Surrender Value and Special Surrender Value depend on years paid and plan rules.

items.q: Is Jeevan Anand maturity taxable under Section 10(10D)?
items.a: Generally tax-free under 10(10D) subject to conditions (e.g., premium limits). Consult a tax advisor for your specific case.

items.q: Should I surrender or make my policy paid-up?
items.a: Paid-up often yields higher final benefit for long-term policies, while surrender gives immediate cash. Use the calculator to compare both options.

items.q: Can NRIs buy Jeevan Anand and use this calculator?
items.a: NRIs can use the calculator; actual purchase eligibility depends on LIC rules and FEMA regulations — check with LIC/agent.

items.q: How does adding riders affect maturity?
items.a: Riders increase premium but typically do not change the maturity sum assured; rider benefits are payable separately on events covered.

items.q: Can I take a loan against Jeevan Anand?
items.a: Yes — loans are generally available after acquiring surrender value, commonly up to 80–90% of the Special Surrender Value.

items.q: How much do bonuses really affect the maturity?
items.a: Massively. They are the engine of your returns. Even a small change in the bonus rate per ₹1,000 Sum Assured compounds over the term and can change your final payout by lakhs. That's why using realistic rates is so important.

items.q: What documents are needed to surrender a Jeevan Anand policy?
items.a: You'll need the original policy bond, a filled surrender form (Form 5074), your identity proof (PAN/Aadhaar), and a cancelled cheque for your bank details. Always confirm the latest list with LIC.

items.q: What is the survival benefit in LIC Jeevan Anand?
items.a: Unlike a money-back plan, Jeevan Anand (915) does not have periodic 'survival benefits'. The main payout is the lump sum at the end of the policy term. However, the life cover continues even after maturity, which is a unique feature.

items.q: How to change nominee in LIC Jeevan Anand online?
items.a: Currently, changing the nominee for an LIC policy is an offline process. You need to fill out the 'Nominee Change Form' and submit it at your servicing LIC branch along with a copy of your policy and KYC documents.

items.q: What is the policy term in LIC Jeevan Anand?
items.a: The policy term is the duration for which you pay premiums and are covered for the primary benefits. For Plan 715, it can range from 15 to 35 years. A unique feature is that the life cover (equal to the Sum Assured) continues even after the policy term, until the policyholder's death.
